Latin word

lēgitimus

lēgitimus, lēgitima, lēgitimum

adjective · Declension on Wiktionary

lawful, legal: fixed or allowed by law; of the law, legal (of questions and terms)

In this lexicon

  • legal

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 25.2.6: quod nōndum ad petendum lēgitima aetās esset; Traupman 196, 339: legal

  • legal

    also used · classical · Quint. 3.6.72 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. legal (related to law or the legal system)

Examples

  • huic petentī aedīlitātem cum obsisterent tribūnī plēbis, negantēs ratiōnem ejus habendam esse quod nōndum ad petendum lēgitima aetās esset, sī mē, inquit, omnēs Quirītēs aedīlem facere volunt, satis annōrum habeō

    When the tribunes of the people opposed his standing for the aedileship, saying he could not be considered because he was not yet of the legal age to stand, he said: “If all the citizens want to make me aedile, I am old enough.”Liv. 25.2.6–7
